<module id="multi_pipe_8bit">
    <description>Design an 8-bit multiplier using pipelined processing. Implement sequential logic for input control, input registers, partial product generation, partial sum calculation, and final product calculation. Ensure proper synchronization and output assignment.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal.</input>
        <input id="mul_en_in">Input enable signal for multiplication operation.</input>
        <input id="mul_a" width_description="[7:0]">Multiplicand input signal.</input>
        <input id="mul_b" width_description="[7:0]">Multiplier input signal.</input>
        <output id="mul_en_out">Output enable signal for multiplication operation.</output>
        <output id="mul_out" width_description="[15:0]">Product output signal.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="IDLE">State IDLE.</parameter>
        <parameter id="LOAD">State LOAD.</parameter>
        <parameter id="CALCULATE">State CALCULATE.</parameter>
        <parameter id="OUTPUT">State OUTPUT.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="mul_en_out_reg" width_description="[3:0]">Register to hold the output enable signal for multiplication operation.</reg>
        <reg id="mul_a_reg" width_description="[7:0]">Register to hold the multiplicand input signal.</reg>
        <reg id="mul_b_reg" width_description="[7:0]">Register to hold the multiplier input signal.</reg>
        <reg id="temp[0]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the first partial product.</reg>
        <reg id="temp[1]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the second partial product.</reg>
        <reg id="temp[2]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the third partial product.</reg>
        <reg id="temp[3]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the fourth partial product.</reg>
        <reg id="temp[4]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the fifth partial product.</reg>
        <reg id="temp[5]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the sixth partial product.</reg>
        <reg id="temp[6]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the seventh partial product.</reg>
        <reg id="temp[7]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the eighth partial product.</reg>
        <reg id="sum[0]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the first partial sum.</reg>
        <reg id="sum[1]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the second partial sum.</reg>
        <reg id="sum[2]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the third partial sum.</reg>
        <reg id="sum[3]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the fourth partial sum.</reg>
        <reg id="sum[4]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the fifth partial sum.</reg>
        <reg id="sum[5]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the sixth partial sum.</reg>
        <reg id="sum[6]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the seventh partial sum.</reg>
        <reg id="sum[7]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the eighth partial sum.</reg>
        <reg id="mul_out_reg" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the final product output.</reg>
        
        // Sequential logic for input control
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                mul_en_out_reg <= 4'd0;
            end else begin
                mul_en_out_reg <= {mul_en_out_reg[2:0], mul_en_in};
            end
        end
        
        // Sequential logic for input registers
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                mul_a_reg <= 8'd0;
                mul_b_reg <= 8'd0;
            end else if (mul_en_in) begin
                mul_a_reg <= mul_a;
                mul_b_reg <= mul_b;
            end
        end
        
        // Combinational logic for partial product generation
        genvar i;
        generate
            for (i = 0; i < 8; i = i + 1) begin : pp_gen
                assign temp[i][15:0] = ({8{mul_b_reg[i]}} & mul_a_reg);
            end
        endgenerate
        
        // Sequential logic for partial sum calculation
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                sum[0] <= 16'd0;
                sum[1] <= 16'd0;
                sum[2] <= 16'd0;
                sum[3] <= 16'd0;
                sum[4] <= 16'd0;
                sum[5] <= 16'd0;
                sum[6] <= 16'd0;
                sum[7] <= 16'd0;
            end else begin
                sum[0] <= temp[0];
                sum[1] <= temp[1] + temp[2];
                sum[2] <= temp[3] + temp[4];
                sum[3] <= temp[5] + temp[6];
                sum[4] <= temp[7];
                sum[5] <= sum[1] + sum[2];
                sum[6] <= sum[3] + sum[4];
                sum[7] <= sum[5] + sum[6];
            end
        end
        
        // Sequential logic for final product calculation
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                mul_out_reg <= 16'd0;
            end else begin
                mul_out_reg <= sum[0] + sum[7];
            end
        end
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>Sequential logic for input control, input registers, partial product generation, partial sum calculation, and final product calculation.</implementation>
    <task>
        <step>Sample the input enable signal and store it in a register.</step>
        <step>Update the input registers with the input values when the input enable signal is active.</step>
        <step>Generate partial products by performing bitwise operations between the multiplicand and the individual bits of the multiplier.</step>
        <step>Calculate partial sums by adding the generated partial products.</step>
        <step>Sum up all the partial sums to obtain the final product.</step>
        <step>Assign the output product value based on the output enable signal.</step>
    </task>
</module>
